sql: lvl_2_id, lvl_3_id, lvl_4_id, lvl_5_id, lvl_6_id, lvl_7_id, lvl_2_id_fn, lvl_3_id_fn, lvl_4_id_fn, lvl_5_id_fn, lvl_6_id_fn, lvl_7_id_fn = {manager_id}
description: Every associate whose reporting chain (lvl_2_id..lvl_7_id) OR functional chain (lvl_2_id_fn..lvl_7_id_fn) contains the manager.
Unless a question says 'weekly', a pay period is a biweekly row of pay_period_dim (freq_cd = 'B').

phrases: current biweekly pay period;current pay period
description: The single biweekly pay period whose is_current_flag is TRUE.

phrases: last {n} pay periods;past {n} pay periods;over the last {n} pay periods
description: A window of N biweekly periods ending at the current one (period_seq -(N-1)..0 inclusive).

phrases: {n} pay periods ago;{n} biweekly pay periods ago
description: The single biweekly pay period N periods before the current one (period_seq = -N).

phrases: {n} to {m} pay-periods-ago;{n} to {m} pay periods ago;{n} to {m} pay-periods-ago window
description: The range of biweekly periods between N and M periods ago, inclusive (period_seq BETWEEN -M AND -N).

phrases: a year ago;compared to a year ago
description: Shorthand for 26 biweekly pay periods ago — the single period at period_seq = -26.

phrases: authoritative snapshot;authoritative current snap;authoritative current snapshot
description: The snapshot taken on the period's own period_end_date (snap_dt equal to the period's ppe_dt).
An authoritative snapshot row whose new_hire_ind is 1. Counting a new hire in a window additionally requires hire_date in the window (see hire_date source).

hire_dt is read from hr.employee_dim (system of record) for EVERY use — window checks, hire-vs-term comparisons, tenure ranking. The snapshot's own hire_dt reflects only what was known at that period's close and MUST NOT be used as the authoritative value.
term_dt is read from hr.employee_dim for EVERY use. The snapshot's own term_dt reflects only what was known at that period's close.
An authoritative snapshot row is active when status_cd = 'A'. NULL / 'L' / 'T' / 'R' / 'U' are NOT active.
An authoritative snapshot row is on leave when status_cd = 'L'. NULL status is unknown (not on leave); every other status is not on leave either.

phrases: not on leave;currently not on leave;NOT on leave
description: Every row where status_cd is NOT 'L', INCLUDING rows where status_cd is NULL.
A turnover row (turn_filt_ind=1) with invol_exit_ind = 0 is voluntary. invol_exit_ind is meaningful only on turnover rows; always check turn_filt_ind = 1.
A turnover row (turn_filt_ind=1) with invol_exit_ind = 1 is involuntary. invol_exit_ind is meaningful only on turnover rows; always check turn_filt_ind = 1.

phrases: unknown invol classification;unknown voluntary/involuntary;voluntary/involuntary classification is unknown
description: A turnover row (turn_filt_ind=1) with NULL invol_exit_ind is the UNKNOWN bucket — reported separately from voluntary and involuntary, and omitted from them.
An associate whose employment type is 'Contractor'.
An associate whose employment type is anything other than 'Contractor', INCLUDING rows where assoc_type is NULL (unknown).
The associate's employment type is stored in the snapshot's assoc_type column. Values: 'FTE', 'Contractor', 'Intern' or NULL for unknown.

sql: ROWS BETWEEN ({n}-1) PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
description: The current row and the N-1 before it, as a window frame on an already-ordered series.
A snapshot row that marks an exit event (turn_filt_ind = 1).
The top N dense ranks: ties kept, no rank skipped.
Documentation only: this suite has no deleted_at column. A terminated associate (status_cd = 'T') is NOT a soft-delete and still appears on authoritative snapshots.
Documentation only: an authoritative-snap associate row across periods. Give it a sql to have it checked.
